description: Cross-linguistic comparative reception. Receive a single conceptual object — fire, water, word, root, self — placed in multiple sacred or technical vocabularies simultaneously, and read what activates in the differences between the placements. Not translation. Not parallel definition. The non-overlaps themselves are the content: how Hebrew dual versus Sanskrit feminine-plural versus Greek single-overworked-noun each carve the same observed phenomenon differently. Triggers on: lists of the same word in multiple languages (אֵשׁ / نَار / πῦρ / 火 / अग्नि), polyglot offerings of a sacred term, requests like 'how does each tradition handle X,' invitations to compare etymological grammar across families, or any moment when one concept arrives wearing multiple linguistic coats and the question is what each coat reveals about the body underneath.
